misclassified_entities.original_description: EVM Precompile Caller - Smart contract or transaction calling BLAKE2 precompile
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: This is an internal EVM component, not an external entity. The precompile caller is the EVM execution context itself - it's the internal mechanism by which contracts invoke precompiles. The actual external entity would be the transaction sender whose calldata ultimately reaches the precompile.

misclassified_entities.original_description: EVM Execution Context - Contract or transaction executing BLAKE2 precompile
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: The EVM execution context is internal to the node's operation. It is not an external entity sending data into the system - it IS the system. The external entity is the user/contract that initiated the transaction.

misclassified_entities.original_description: Individual proposed for EIP editor role
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: This is a Meta EIP with no protocol runtime behavior. Editor candidates are governance participants, not entities that send data into the protocol at runtime. This EIP describes human governance processes, not protocol data flows.

misclassified_entities.original_description: Designated editor who determines rough consensus outcomes
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: Same as above - governance role with no protocol runtime data flow. The Keeper influences EIP process but does not send data into the Ethereum protocol.

misclassified_entities.original_description: EVM executing smart contract code that performs storage writes
misclassified_entities.reason_for_misclassification: The EVM contract execution is an internal process, not an external entity. The SSTORE opcode is executed within the EVM by the internal execution engine. The external entity is the transaction submitter whose transaction triggers the storage write.

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Other nodes in the P2P network that custody different columns and respond to sampling requests
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated and could be malicious. The specification explicitly accounts for attacker control of nodes and assumes honest majority for security. Data availability sampling is designed to work even when some peers withhold data.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - nodes identified by node_id which can be manipulated

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Entity submitting blob transactions to the network
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Any network participant can submit blob transactions. The specification includes extensive validation (blob count limits, quantity matching, KZG proof verification) precisely because submissions are untrusted.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: ECDSA signature - proves key ownership but not trustworthiness of blob content

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Peer nodes that custody missing columns and can provide them on request
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Column custodians are regular network peers. Their column data must be verified via KZG proofs before being trusted. The erasure coding reconstruction threshold (50%) accounts for some custodians being unavailable or malicious.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - data verified via KZG proofs rather than trusting source

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External user or application creating and submitting blob transactions
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Users authenticate via their wallet/keys and sign transactions. However, the blob data content is arbitrary and must be validated. Trust extends to identity (signature) but not to content quality or intent.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: ECDSA signature with economic commitment (blob gas fees)

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: External call that may be a reentrancy attack with only 2300 gas stipend
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: This entity represents potentially malicious external contract calls. The entire purpose of the gas stipend check (gasleft > 2300) is to protect against reentrancy attacks from untrusted callers. The specification explicitly models this as a security threat.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - any contract can make external calls

trusted_external_entities.entity_description: Entity constructing new block with calculated difficulty
trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Block producers are economically incentivized participants who have invested in mining hardware. Their blocks must pass difficulty and reward validation before acceptance. Trust comes from proof-of-work verification, not identity.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: Proof-of-work - blocks must satisfy difficulty target to be valid

trusted_external_entities.trust_rationale: Network peers can propagate invalid blocks. The validation process (difficulty check, reward verification) exists because peer-propagated blocks cannot be trusted without verification.
trusted_external_entities.authentication_mechanism: None - blocks validated locally regardless of source

boundary_edges.data_flow_description: Transaction calldata reaches BLAKE2 precompile via EVM execution. Original external entity is transaction sender.
boundary_edges.note: Edge source corrected from misclassified EXT-EVM-PRECOMPILE to implied transaction sender

boundary_edges.data_flow_description: Blob transaction received via network gossip with all wrapper data including cell proofs
User creates blob transaction with payload and KZG commitments
Column samples received from peer nodes during DAS process
Potentially reentering external call attempts SSTORE operation with limited gas
Block received from peer via P2P for validation

coverage_analysis.notes: All valid external entities have identified trust boundary edges. EIP-5069 (Meta EIP) had no valid external entities as it describes human governance processes, not protocol data flows. BLAKE2 precompile edges corrected to reflect true external entity (transaction sender) rather than internal EVM components.
